name: Nek
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: OLAC (nif) lists only literacy booklets, wordlists, and the Retsema/Potter/Gray 2009 SIL survey; no phonology description located.

sources.citation: Claassen, O. R. & K. A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range, New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11 (Pacific Linguistics A-23), 45-78.
sources.note: Sec. 6.1 (pp. 63-67) sketches phonologies of Yaganon, Suroi, Evapia, Rawa, Yupna, Uruwa, Wantoat and Uri; the only stress sentence (p. 66) is 'Stress is phonemic in Rawa but probably sub-phonemic in Yupna and Wantoat... In Suroi stress is contrastive, but only on a limited number of words.' Nek appears only in the classification (sec. 2.7.10, p. 58: 1300 speakers north of Boana, W dialect 96% related to E). No Nek or Erap stress data.

sources.citation: nektokmedia.com. 2024. Nek Language (community site: alphabet page, about page, literacy books, picture dictionary).
sources.note: Alphabet a, b, d, e, f, g, gw, i, ɨ, j, k, kw, l, m, n, ŋ, o, p, s, t, u, w, y; two dialects (East/West); no grammar or phonology document, nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Yunamu, Kaik & Isolde Kappus (adapted from Linnasalo, Katri & Gonte Bayam 2006). 2024. Kisim save long ritim Nek Wes [Tok Pisin-to-Nek West transfer primer]. Ukarumpa: SIL PNG. 34 pp.
sources.note: Literacy primer in Tok Pisin; explains letters and digraphs (ŋ, ɨ, kw, gw, j) but nothing on word stress. On ɨ (p. 26): 'yumi no ken kolim strong... yumi mas kolim kwiktaim' (the vowel is weak/short), not a stress rule.

sources.citation: McElhanon, K. A. 1973. Towards a typology of the Finisterre-Huon languages, New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-22.

sources.note: Ch. 1 Phonology (pp. 5-8) compares phoneme inventories, syllable structure and morphophonemics of ten representative languages (Uri represents Erap); no stress or accent section; Nek only listed as Erap family member (p. 2).
Stub with no phonology; cites only Ethnologue and nektokmedia.com.
